insight.title: Why You Communicate Worse With People You Know Well
insight.subtitle: Why being close to someone can make you harder to understand

sections.text: You likely assume your inner circle can read your mind. But research shows we often communicate more vaguely with those we love than with strangers, leading to avoidable friction and constant missed expectations.

This "Closeness-Communication Bias" happens because your brain skips providing context. You subconsciously assume they already have the "key" to your thoughts, even when they are operating with entirely different information than you are.
In meetings or at home, this creates a false sense of transparency. You feel you’ve been crystal clear, but they are left guessing. Familiarity is a poor substitute for actual precision.
Try this today: The next time you ask someone close for something today, provide one extra sentence of context.
Clarity is a gift you often forget to give to the people who matter most.
